title_en: Law on Medical Practitioners of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of physicians, regulating physicians' practice, strengthening the building of the physician workforce, protecting people's health, and advancing the construction of a Healthy China.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "physicians" mean professional medical personnel who have obtained physician qualifications according to law and are registered to practice in medical and health institutions, including practicing physicians and practicing assistant physicians.

Article 3 Physicians shall adhere to putting the people and life above all else, carry forward the humanitarian spirit, promote the noble professional spirit of respecting and protecting life, healing the wounded and rescuing the dying, being willing to contribute, and having boundless love, abide by professional ethics, comply with practice standards, improve their practice level, and fulfill the sacred duty of preventing and treating diseases and protecting people's health.
Physicians who practice according to law shall be protected by law. The personal dignity and personal safety of physicians shall not be violated.

Article 4 The health administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the administration of physicians nationwide. The education, human resources and social security, traditional Chinese medicine and other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for the relevant administration of physicians within their respective functions and duties.
The health administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the administration of physicians within their respective administrative regions. The education, human resources and social security, traditional Chinese medicine and other relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the relevant administration of physicians within their respective functions and duties.

Article 5 August 19 of each year shall be the Chinese Physicians' Day.
Physicians who have made outstanding contributions in the work of medical and health services shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
The whole society shall respect physicians. People's governments at all levels shall care for and protect physicians, promote their advanced deeds, strengthen professional training, support innovation and pioneering, help solve difficulties, and promote the formation of a good atmosphere of respecting physicians and valuing health throughout society.

Article 6 The State shall establish and improve the system for the establishment, evaluation and appointment of physicians' medical professional and technical titles, taking professional ethics, professional practice ability and work performance as important conditions, and scientifically setting relevant evaluation and appointment standards.

Article 7 Physicians may, according to law, organize and participate in relevant industry organizations such as physicians' associations and professional academic groups.
Relevant industry organizations such as physicians' associations shall strengthen industry self-discipline and physicians' practice standards, safeguard the lawful rights and interests of physicians, and assist the health administrative department and other relevant departments in carrying out relevant work.

Article 8 The State shall implement a system of physician qualification examinations.
The physician qualification examinations shall be divided into the practicing physician qualification examination and the practicing assistant physician qualification examination. The physician qualification examinations shall be organized and implemented by the health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the provincial level.
The categories and specific measures for the physician qualification examinations shall be formulated by the health administrative department of the State Council.

Article 9 A person who meets any of the following conditions may take the practicing physician qualification examination:
(1) Having a bachelor's degree or above in a relevant medical specialty from an institution of higher education, and having participated in medical professional work practice in a medical and health institution under the guidance of a practicing physician for at least one year; or
(2) Having an associate degree in a relevant medical specialty from an institution of higher education, and having practiced in a medical and health institution for at least two years after obtaining the practice certificate of a practicing assistant physician.

Article 10 A person who has an associate degree or above in a relevant medical specialty from an institution of higher education and has participated in medical professional work practice in a medical and health institution under the guidance of a practicing physician for at least one year may take the practicing assistant physician qualification examination.

Article 11 A person who has studied traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) under a master for at least three years, or who has genuinely specialized medical skills through many years of practice, may take the TCM physician qualification examination after passing the assessment conducted by a TCM professional organization or a medical and health institution entrusted by the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level and being recommended thereby.
A person who has studied TCM under a master or through many years of practice and has genuinely specialized medical skills may, after being recommended by at least two TCM physicians and passing the practical skills and effectiveness assessment organized by the TCM administrative department of the provincial people's government, obtain the TCM physician qualification and the corresponding qualification certificate.
The relevant examination and assessment measures provided for in this Article shall be drafted by the TCM administrative department of the State Council, and submitted to the health administrative department of the State Council for review and promulgation.

Article 12 A person who passes the physician qualification examination and obtains the practicing physician qualification or the practicing assistant physician qualification shall be issued a physician qualification certificate.

Article 13 The State shall implement a system of physician practice registration.
A person who has obtained a physician qualification may apply for registration to the health administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level where he or she is located. A medical and health institution may handle the registration procedures collectively for the applicants in that institution.
Unless there are circumstances under which registration shall be refused as provided for in this Law, the health administrative department shall grant registration within twenty working days from the date of accepting the application, enter the registration information into the national information platform, and issue a physician practice certificate.
No person shall engage in physician practice activities without being registered and obtaining a physician practice certificate.
The specific measures for the administration of physician practice registration shall be formulated by the health administrative department of the State Council.

Article 14 After registration, a physician may practice in a medical and health institution in accordance with the registered practice location, practice category, and practice scope, and engage in corresponding medical and health services.
A physician of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) or integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine may practice in the TCM department, integrated TCM and Western medicine department, or other clinical departments of a medical institution in accordance with the registered practice category and practice scope.
A physician may add a practice scope after completing relevant professional training and passing the assessment. Where laws or administrative regulations provide for the qualification conditions for a physician to engage in practice activities in a specific scope, such provisions shall prevail.
A TCM physician who has obtained physician qualifications through examination may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and after completing training and passing the assessment, adopt Western medicine technical methods related to his or her specialty in practice activities. A Western medicine physician may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and after completing training and passing the assessment, adopt TCM technical methods related to his or her specialty in practice activities.

Article 15 Where a physician practices regularly in two or more medical and health institutions, he or she shall take one medical and health institution as the main practice institution and go through the relevant procedures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. The State encourages physicians to regularly and at designated points provide medical and health services in medical and health institutions below the county level, including township health centers, village clinics, community health service centers, etc. The main practice institution shall support and provide convenience.
The health administrative departments and medical and health institutions shall strengthen the supervision and administration of such physicians, regulate their practice behaviors, and ensure the quality of medical and health services.

Article 18 Where a physician changes the registered items such as practice location, practice category, or practice scope, he or she shall undergo the registration modification procedures with the health administrative department that granted the registration in accordance with the provisions of this Law.
A physician may not undergo the relevant registration modification procedures when engaging in any of the following activities:
(1) Participating in standardized training, advanced studies, paired assistance, consultation, medical rescue in emergencies, charitable or other public welfare medical care, or free clinics;
(2) Undertaking national tasks or participating in important activities organized by the government; or
(3) Practicing in a medical institution within a medical consortium.

Article 19 A person who has suspended physician practice activities for more than two years, or whose circumstances for which registration was refused under this Law have ceased to exist, and who applies for re-practice, shall pass the assessment conducted by the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level or a medical and health institution or an industry organization entrusted thereby, and shall be re-registered in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 20 A physician who practices medicine individually shall undergo the approval or record-filing procedures according to law.
A practicing physician who practices medicine individually must have practiced in a medical and health institution for at least five years after registration; however, a person who has obtained the TCM physician qualification in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 11 of this Law may practice medicine individually within the registered practice scope after undergoing practice registration based on the assessment content.
The health administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall carry out supervision and inspection over physicians who practice medicine individually in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and if it discovers any circumstance for which registration shall be cancelled as provided for in this Law, it shall promptly cancel the registration and revoke the physician practice certificate.

Article 21 The health administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall promptly announce the list of persons who have been granted registration and whose registration has been cancelled. The health administrative departments of provincial people's governments shall compile the lists and report them to the health administrative department of the State Council for record, and shall provide inquiry services for physician registration information through websites in accordance with the provisions.

Article 24 When implementing medical, prevention, or health care measures and signing relevant medical certificates, a physician must personally conduct diagnosis and investigation, and timely fill in medical documents such as medical records in accordance with the provisions, and shall not conceal, forge, alter, or arbitrarily destroy medical documents such as medical records and related materials.
A physician shall not issue false medical certificates or medical certificates that are unrelated to his or her practice scope or inconsistent with his or her practice category.

Article 25 In diagnosis and treatment activities, a physician shall explain to the patient the condition, medical measures, and other matters that need to be informed. Where surgery, special examination, or special treatment is required, the physician shall promptly explain in detail to the patient the medical risks, alternative treatment plans, and other circumstances, and obtain the patient's explicit consent; where it is impossible or inappropriate to explain to the patient, the physician shall explain to the patient's close relatives and obtain their explicit consent.

Article 26 A physician who conducts clinical trials of drugs or medical devices or other medical clinical research shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State, abide by medical ethics norms, pass ethical review according to law, and obtain written informed consent.

Article 27 For patients requiring emergency treatment, a physician shall take emergency measures for diagnosis and treatment and shall not refuse emergency treatment.
In an emergency situation such as rescuing a patient who is critically ill, where consent cannot be obtained from the patient or his or her close relatives, upon approval of the person in charge of the medical institution or an authorized person, the corresponding medical measures may be implemented immediately.
The State encourages physicians to actively participate in first aid services in public places such as public transportation; a physician who causes damage to a recipient due to voluntary first aid shall not bear civil liability.

Article 28 A physician shall use drugs, disinfectants, and medical devices that have been approved or filed according to law, and adopt lawful, compliant, and scientific diagnosis and treatment methods.
Except for use in diagnosis and treatment in accordance with standards, no narcotic drugs, toxic drugs for medical use, psychotropic drugs, or radioactive drugs shall be used.

Article 29 A physician shall adhere to the principle of safe, effective, economical, and rational medication use, and follow the guiding principles for clinical application of drugs, clinical diagnosis and treatment guidelines, drug instructions, and other standards for rational drug use.
Under special circumstances such as when there is no effective or better treatment method, after obtaining the patient's explicit informed consent, a physician may adopt a drug usage method that is not specified in the drug instructions but has evidence-based medical evidence for treatment. Medical institutions shall establish management systems to review the appropriateness of physicians' prescriptions and medication orders, and strictly regulate physicians' medication behavior.

Article 30 A practicing physician may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and with the consent of the medical and health institution where he or she works, provide appropriate medical and health services such as follow-up consultations for some common diseases and chronic diseases through information technologies such as the Internet. The State supports medical and health institutions in using information technologies such as the Internet to carry out telemedicine cooperation.

Article 31 A physician shall not, by taking advantage of his or her position, demand or illegally accept property or seek other illegitimate benefits; shall not perform unnecessary examinations or treatments on patients.

Article 32 When encountering emergencies such as natural disasters, accident disasters, public health incidents, and social security incidents that seriously threaten people's lives and health, the health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall organize physicians to participate in health emergency response and medical treatment as needed, and physicians shall obey the dispatch.

Article 34 A practicing assistant physician shall practice in a medical and health institution under the guidance of a practicing physician and in accordance with the registered practice category and practice scope.
A practicing assistant physician who practices in a medical and health institution in a township, ethnic township, town, or village, or in a county-level medical and health institution in a difficult and remote area may independently engage in general practice activities based on the medical and health service situation and his or her own practical experience.

Article 35 Medical students participating in clinical teaching practice and medical graduates who have not yet obtained a physician practice certificate and are participating in medical professional work practice in a medical and health institution shall participate in clinical diagnosis and treatment activities under the supervision and guidance of a practicing physician. Medical and health institutions shall provide the necessary conditions for such medical students and medical graduates to participate in clinical diagnosis and treatment activities.

Article 36 Relevant industry organizations, medical and health institutions, and medical schools shall strengthen the education of physicians in medical ethics and professional conduct.
Medical and health institutions shall establish and improve systems such as physician post responsibilities, internal supervision, and complaint handling, and strengthen the management of physicians.

Article 37 The State shall formulate plans for physician training, establish a physician training and supply-demand balance mechanism that adapts to the characteristics of the industry and social needs, coordinate the demand for various types of medical talents, and strengthen the training of professionals in shortage areas such as general practice, pediatrics, psychiatry, and geriatrics.
The State shall take measures to strengthen the coordination of medical education, and improve the systems of medical school education, postgraduate education, and continuing education.
The State shall strengthen the cultivation and deployment of primary-level medical and health talents, with a focus on general practitioners, through various channels.
The State shall take measures to improve the education system for mutual learning between traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Western medicine, and cultivate high-level integrated TCM and Western medicine talents and general practitioners capable of providing integrated TCM and Western medicine services.

Article 38 The State shall establish and improve the standardized training system for resident physicians, improve the incentive mechanism for clinical teaching, guarantee the treatment of resident physicians during training, and strictly manage the training process and the final assessment.
The State shall establish and improve the standardized training system for specialist physicians, and continuously improve the specialist diagnosis and treatment level of clinical physicians.

Article 39 The health administrative departments and other relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall formulate physician training plans, provide graded and categorized training for physicians in various forms, and provide conditions for physicians to receive continuing medical education.
People's governments at or above the county level shall take effective measures to give priority to ensuring that medical and health personnel in primary-level, underdeveloped areas, and ethnic minority areas receive continuing medical education.

Article 40 Medical and health institutions shall reasonably allocate human resources, and ensure that physicians in their institutions receive continuing medical education in accordance with the provisions and plans.
The health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, in a planned manner, organize and coordinate medical and health institutions at or above the county level to provide training for medical and health personnel in primary-level medical and health institutions such as township health centers, village clinics, and community health service centers, so as to improve their medical professional technical ability and level.
Relevant industry organizations shall provide services and create conditions for physicians to receive continuing medical education, and strengthen the organization and management of continuing medical education.

Article 41 The State shall, in the annual enrollment plan for medical specialties and the education and training plan, allocate a certain proportion for targeted training and entrusted training, so as to strengthen the construction of the physician workforce in primary-level and difficult and remote areas.
Relevant departments and medical and health institutions shall sign agreements with persons receiving targeted training or entrusted training, specifying matters such as relevant treatment, service years, and liability for breach of contract. The persons concerned shall perform the obligations stipulated in the agreements. The relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to strengthen the management of performance of the agreements. Any party to an agreement that violates the agreement shall bear liability for breach of contract.

Article 42 The State shall implement a system of regular assessment of physicians.
The health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level, or the medical and health institutions or industry organizations entrusted by them, shall assess physicians' professional level, work performance, and professional ethics status in accordance with the physician practice standards, with an assessment cycle of three years. For physicians with a long practice experience and no record of不良 conduct, the assessment procedures may be simplified.
The entrusted institution or organization shall report the assessment results of physicians to the health administrative department that granted the registration for record.
For a physician who fails the assessment, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order him or her to suspend practice activities for a period of three to six months and receive relevant professional training. Upon expiration of the suspension period, a reassessment shall be conducted. If the physician passes the reassessment, he or she shall be allowed to continue practicing.
Article 43 The health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the provincial level shall be responsible for guiding, inspecting, and supervising the assessment of physicians.

Article 44 The State shall establish and improve personnel, remuneration, professional title, and reward systems that reflect the professional characteristics and technical labor value of physicians.
Physicians engaged in the prevention and control of infectious diseases, radiology, mental health, and other special positions shall be given appropriate allowances in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. The allowance standards shall be adjusted periodically.
Physicians working in primary-level and difficult and remote areas shall enjoy allowance and subsidy policies in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and enjoy preferential treatment in terms of professional title evaluation, career development, education and training, and commendation and reward.

Article 45 The State shall strengthen the construction of the disease prevention and control talent team, and establish a mechanism for the training and use of physicians that adapts to a modern disease prevention and control system.
Disease prevention and control institutions, medical institutions at or above the second level, and primary-level medical and health institutions such as township health centers and community health service centers shall be equipped with a certain number of public health physicians to engage in public health work such as monitoring of population diseases and risk factors, risk assessment and analysis, monitoring and early warning, epidemiological investigation, immunization program management, and occupational health management. Medical institutions shall establish and improve management systems and strictly implement infection prevention and control measures within the institutions.
The State shall establish a talent training mechanism combining public health and clinical medicine, provide business training on disease prevention and control and response to public health emergencies for clinical physicians through various channels, provide clinical medical business training for public health physicians, and improve the system and mechanism for the combination of medical treatment and prevention and the coordinated prevention and treatment of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine.

Article 46 The State shall take measures to coordinate urban and rural resources, strengthen the construction of the primary-level medical and health team and service capacity, establish a career development mechanism connecting counties, townships, and villages for rural medical and health personnel, and incorporate rural medical and health personnel into county-level medical and health personnel management through methods such as county management and township use, and township employment and village use.
A practicing physician who is to be promoted to the deputy senior technical title shall have a cumulative experience of at least one year in providing medical and health services in a medical and health institution below the county level or in a paired assistance medical and health institution; after being promoted to the deputy senior technical title, if the physician has provided medical and health services in a medical and health institution below the county level or in a paired assistance medical and health institution for a cumulative period of at least one year, he or she shall be given priority for promotion to the senior technical title under the same conditions.
The State shall take measures to encourage persons who have obtained the practicing physician qualification or practicing assistant physician qualification to establish village medical and health institutions according to law, or to provide medical and health services in village medical and health institutions.

Article 47 The State encourages village doctors who provide prevention, health care, and general medical services to villagers in village medical and health institutions to obtain medical professional degrees through medical education; encourages qualified village doctors to take physician qualification examinations and obtain physician qualifications according to law.
The State shall take measures to help village doctors improve their medical technical ability and level through information technology and intelligent means, and further improve the multi-channel subsidy mechanism for village doctors' service income and policies such as old-age care.
The specific measures for the administration of village doctors shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 49 People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall incorporate the prevention and handling of medical disputes into the comprehensive social security management system, strengthen the comprehensive management of public security around medical and health institutions, maintain a good practice environment in medical and health institutions, effectively prevent and combat illegal and criminal acts involving medical treatment according to law, and protect the lawful rights and interests of both medical personnel and patients.
Medical and health institutions shall improve security measures, maintain good medical order, promptly and proactively resolve medical disputes, and ensure the safety of physicians' practice.
No organization or individual shall obstruct physicians from practicing according to law or interfere with physicians' normal work and life; no organization or individual shall violate physicians' personal dignity or personal safety through means such as insult, defamation, threat, or assault.

Article 50 Medical and health institutions shall provide physicians with occupational safety and health protection supplies, and take effective health protection and medical care measures.
A physician who suffers an accident injury or contracts a disease or dies due to exposure to toxic or harmful factors in occupational activities shall enjoy work-related injury insurance benefits in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 51 Medical and health institutions shall reasonably arrange working hours for physicians, implement the paid leave system, and conduct regular health examinations.

Article 52 The State shall establish and improve a medical risk sharing mechanism. Medical institutions shall participate in medical liability insurance or establish and participate in medical risk funds. Patients are encouraged to participate in medical accident insurance.

Article 53 News media shall carry out public interest publicity on medical and health laws, regulations, and medical and health knowledge, promote the advanced deeds of physicians, and guide the public to respect physicians and deal with medical and health risks rationally.

Article 54 Where a person violates examination discipline or commits other acts in the physician qualification examination, if the circumstances are serious, the person shall be prohibited from taking the physician qualification examination for one to three years.
Where a person obtains a physician qualification certificate or a physician practice certificate by improper means, the health administrative department that issued the certificate shall revoke it, and shall not accept the corresponding application for three years.
Where a person forges, alters, buys, sells, leases, or lends a physician practice certificate, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than 10,000 yuan, the calculation shall be based on 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the physician practice certificate shall be revoked.

Article 57 Where a physician, in violation of this Law, practices at a practice location, in a practice category, or within a practice scope not in accordance with the registration, the health administrative department or the traditional Chinese medicine administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction, give a warning, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the department shall order suspension of practice for not less than six months but not more than one year up to revocation of the physician practice certificate.

Article 58 Where a person seriously violates the professional ethics of physicians and medical ethics norms, causing adverse social impact, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall revoke the physician practice certificate or order cessation of illegal practice activities, and prohibit the person from engaging in medical and health services or medical clinical research for five years up to life.

Article 59 Where a person who is not a physician practices medicine in violation of this Law, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order cessation of illegal practice activities, confiscate the illegal gains, drugs, and medical devices, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than two times but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than 10,000 yuan, the calculation shall be based on 10,000 yuan.

Article 60 Where a person, in violation of this Law, obstructs a physician from practicing according to law, interferes with the physician's normal work and life, or infringes upon the physician's personal dignity and personal safety by means of insult, defamation, threat, assault, etc., which constitutes a violation of public security administration, the person shall be given a public security administration penalty according to law.

Article 61 Where a medical and health institution, in violation of this Law, fails to perform its reporting duties, causing serious consequences, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall give a warning, and the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 62 Where a staff member of the health administrative department or other relevant departments or a staff member of a medical and health institution, in violation of this Law, engages in fraud, abuse of power, dereliction of duty, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, the person shall be given a sanction according to law.

Article 63 Where a violation of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if personal injury or property damage is caused, civil liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 64 The State shall take measures to encourage persons with a medical specialty diploma from a secondary specialized school to improve their medical technical ability and level by participating in higher-level academic education or other means.
Persons who have obtained a relevant medical specialty diploma from a secondary specialized school before the coming into force of this Law and within a certain period after the coming into force of this Law may take the physician qualification examination. Specific measures shall be formulated by the health administrative department of the State Council jointly with the education, traditional Chinese medicine, and other relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 65 Specific measures for the implementation of this Law by the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall be formulated by the State Council and the Central Military Commission in accordance with this Law.

Article 66 Specific administrative measures for overseas personnel to take the physician qualification examination, apply for registration, practice medicine, or engage in clinical teaching, clinical research, clinical academic exchanges, or other activities shall be formulated by the health administrative department of the State Council.
Article 67 This Law shall come into force on March 1, 2022. The Law of the People's Republic of China on Licensed Doctors shall be abolished simultaneously.
